goal: Continuously improve the real mobile UI/UX from user feedback, beginning with war-zone exploration desire while preserving the accepted title and factory-world direction.

player_outcome.target_player: first-time mobile landscape light-SLG player familiar with anime city-war imagery
player_outcome.control: selects a campaign landmark, changes chapter, opens contextual detail, and chooses the primary action
player_outcome.threat: locked frontier, hostile occupied city, and uncertain stage capability
player_outcome.choice: explore the next landmark, prepare the legion, or attack the selected stage
player_outcome.feedback: world-first map, route state, landmark silhouette, selected detail, and one contextual primary action
player_outcome.outcome: understands territorial progression and wants to reveal the next occupied location without searching through UI panels

constraints.asset_policy: original generated or repository-owned raster assets only; no unlicensed copied franchise art
scope: title, factory, war-zone and cross-screen UI/UX challenged by the user's feedback
accessibility: state is encoded by silhouette, icon and position in addition to colour
critical action remains visible at both target viewports

quality_dimensions.label: Assets and modeling
scope: title hero art, map landmark silhouettes, and formation character portraits
quality_dimensions.rationale: The user explicitly challenged character identity and generic AI-looking landmarks.

quality_dimensions.label: Materials, shaders, and lighting
scope: map depth, occupied-city atmosphere and readable value hierarchy
quality_dimensions.rationale: Exploration desire depends on depth and atmosphere rather than flat panels.

quality_dimensions.label: Motion and VFX
quality_dimensions.rationale: This first bounded wave changes static map composition and HUD hierarchy, not temporal VFX.

quality_dimensions.label: UI and UX
scope: title simplicity, factory contextual HUD, war-zone hierarchy, formation identity and feedback flow

quality_dimensions.label: Interaction, camera, and physics
scope: stage selection, chapter navigation and contextual panel actions
quality_dimensions.rationale: The player must manipulate the real shipping screen without blocked map targets.

quality_dimensions.label: Gameplay, levels, and AI
scope: campaign stage availability and attack/preparation routing
quality_dimensions.rationale: Map presentation must remain bound to real campaign state.

quality_dimensions.label: Balance, economy, and progression
quality_dimensions.rationale: No values, costs, rewards or unlock rules are changed.

quality_dimensions.label: Narrative and content
scope: original-inspired occupied-city counterattack atmosphere without copied art
quality_dimensions.rationale: The user explicitly requires a stronger original-world feeling and exploration fantasy.

quality_dimensions.label: Audio
quality_dimensions.rationale: This wave makes no audio claim.

quality_dimensions.label: Learning and replay
scope: two-second territorial progression and desire to inspect the next landmark
quality_dimensions.rationale: Only target-player observation can close the exploration and comprehension claim.

quality_dimensions.label: Accessibility and localization
scope: dual-coded stage state, Chinese text fit and mobile touch size
quality_dimensions.rationale: The target viewports and non-colour state encoding are explicit constraints.

quality_dimensions.label: Correctness, data, and lifecycle
scope: screen rebuild, selection signals, disabled states and repeat navigation
quality_dimensions.rationale: Visual changes must not break the shipping campaign flow.

quality_dimensions.label: Performance and stability
scope: Web-safe map drawing and lightweight raster budget
quality_dimensions.rationale: The accepted candidate must import and run without destabilizing the Web target.

quality_bar.comparison: At 844x390 and 568x320, a blind reviewer can identify recovered territory, the current selectable landmark, and the locked hostile frontier before reading the detail panel.
quality_bar.inspect_route: scenario_war_zone_exploration focused dual-size bundle, followed by scenario_ui_path_integration after the accepted candidate
limits: Static captures and automated routes cannot prove target-player exploration desire, touch feel, or physical-phone safe areas.
